newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian workers hold 28 foreign hostages on barge.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian workers hold 28 foreign hostages on barge.

text.p: Twenty-eight foreigners, including 10 Filipinos and nine Frenchmen, are being held hostage on a barge offshore southeastern Nigeria by 60 Nigerian workers demanding wage increases, a Philippine diplomat said on Friday.

"It is the fifth day today. They have been there since December 23rd and there is ongoing negotiations to resolve the situation," Hermes Dorado, consul-general of the Philippine embassy in Lagos, told Reuters.
The dispute involves a French oil services company identified as NTPM that employed the workers on its barge, the WB-82, which transports crude oil from onshore fields to tankers.
The other hostages are five Indians, two Britons, one Lebanese and one Belgian. The Nigerians on the barge did not appear to have firearms, Dorado said.
"So far they are safe and unharmed despite the passing yesterday of a deadline by the Nigerian workers who said things will happen if their demands were not met by then," he said.
Dorado said the vessel was being held some 50 km (30 miles) offshore from the oil-producing town of Eket.
Mobil Nigeria Unlimited, a joint venture with the U.S. firm Mobil Corp, is the main producer of crude oil in that area but its staff were unavailable to comment on Friday because of public holidays.
Dorado said the Filipino crew sent an urgent message to Manila for help and his government was worried about them.
"Our president has sent us instructions to ensure their safety and we are working on the negotiations with NTPM to ensure it is resolved peacefully," he added.
